$comment: The Lakekeeper dev rig (W109, coordinator 2026-11-27): the catalog the owner chose as the end state if the cutover-gate tests pass (self-hosted open-source Lakekeeper, no Plus), built in dev only to run those tests. infra/aws-lakekeeper-dev reads this file for its names and sizes and config/aws-platform.contract.json for the account, the region, the tags, the state bucket and the platform's network and database. Every name says lakekeeper-dev. Destroyed when the tests are done; the catalog ADR (0624) is written after them.
name: perfectory-lakekeeper-dev

catalog.reason: Lakekeeper v0.15.1 (the version contract's quay.io/lakekeeper/catalog), two tasks so that one can be killed mid-call (T14) and a rolling upgrade can be watched (T16). Fargate's smallest ARM size: Lakekeeper is one Rust process with no local state (upstream production checklist); measure it in the tests and size prod from that. Pools are small because the platform's RDS instance is a db.t4g.micro shared with Dagster, with about 160 MB freeable memory (CloudWatch FreeableMemory minimum, 2026-11-27): each task has a catalog and a secrets pool, each with these read and write sizes, so at most 2 tasks x 2 x (2 + 2) connections; the tests watch that memory. A write pool of 1 deadlocks: creating a warehouse holds one write connection while the secret store waits for another ('pool timed out while waiting for an open connection', 2026-11-27).

authz.reason: OpenFGA v1.14 (the version Lakekeeper v0.15.1 tests against; 1.11 or later is required), its own service so that it can be stopped alone (T7: every call is refused while it is down). One task in dev; Lakekeeper's Helm chart runs as many as catalog replicas. Lakekeeper reaches it by gRPC with a pre-shared key.

databases.reason: Each its own database and login on the platform's RDS instance (coordinator 2026-11-27), never the Dagster or ledger ones. The login owns its database, so its migrations create what they need (Lakekeeper's five extensions are trusted on PostgreSQL 17). Each password is generated at apply time and written write-only, never in the state. The connection limits keep the rig from starving Dagster on the shared instance.

identity.reason: Machine identity is one Cognito app client per principal with the client-credentials flow (coordinator 2026-11-27): Lakekeeper takes OIDC JWTs only and has no AWS IAM login. Lakekeeper admits a token only with the catalog scope, token_use=access and the client_id of a declared principal (its required-claim rules); a Cognito access token carries no aud, so the scope and the client list do what an audience would. bootstrap is the operator the bootstrap/reconciler task runs as; lane-a and lane-b are two lanes (lane-b also holds the other scope and a 5-minute token, for the scope and expiry tests); outsider is a valid token of the same pool that is not declared and must be refused. Each principal's client secret is readable only by its own probe's execution role. App clients of the client-credentials flow cost nothing; a token request costs 0.00225 USD (AWS Price List, ap-northeast-2, 2026-11-27).

warehouse.reason: The one warehouse is the dev bucket, never a prod bucket, named after its bucket, with namespaces silver and gold and tables at <namespace>/<table>/ (concepts brief 'Lakehouse catalog', Q2 and disagreement 5): no key prefix, and a full-hierarchy layout of names only (upstream storage-layout, v0.15.1), which T3 checks. Soft deletion with a 10-minute expiry, so T11a sees undrop and purge in one sitting. region is an R2 location hint, as upstream's R2 section asks. Made by the warehouse task (probes.tf: the operator's probe that alone reads the R2 credential, warehouse.tf), not by OpenTofu: Lakekeeper takes the credential through its API and keeps it encrypted in its own database. Its R2 credential is a new Cloudflare account API token of this rig only, R2 Admin Read & Write (owner decision 2026-11-27, option A; upstream: temp-access-credentials accepts no other), never the existing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN.

reason: Named dev everywhere, in its own state and its own ECS cluster. It reads the platform stack's VPC, public subnets and database by name and adds only ingress rules to the database's security group. The internal endpoint is private DNS (Cloud Map), the way the Dagster code servers are reached: no load balancer (root ADR-0616 §1). Probes run as one-off tasks from inside the VPC, one task definition per principal, and print results, never a secret or a token.
